result.keyword: Which no win no fee compensation lawyers in Melbourne would you recommend?
result.markdown:
Yes. I’d shortlist **4 Melbourne firms** rather than choosing purely on advertising or Google reviews. I checked firms’ current information and the Victorian regulator’s guidance on “no win, no fee” agreements.

### My shortlist

| Firm | Why I’d consider them | Best suited to |
|---|---|---|
| **Law Partners Injury Lawyers Melbourne** | Strong specialist focus on personal injury. They advertise **no win, no fee with no disbursement costs**, and report a 99%+ success rate. [lawpartners.com.au](https://lawpartners.com.au/offices/personal-injury-lawyers-melbourne?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | General personal injury, workplace injuries, accidents |
| **Maurice Blackburn Personal Injury Lawyers Melbourne** | Very established plaintiff-side practice, with broad compensation expertise and no-win-no-fee arrangements. They have particular depth in WorkCover, road accidents and medical negligence. [www.mauriceblackburn.com.au](https://www.mauriceblackburn.com.au/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | **Complex or high-value claims**, WorkCover, medical negligence, road accidents |
| **Shine Lawyers Melbourne** | Large dedicated personal-injury practice. Melbourne office explicitly offers no-win-no-fee and handles TAC, WorkCover, public liability, product liability and medical negligence. [www.shine.com.au](https://www.shine.com.au/locations/vic/melbourne?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | Workplace/WorkCover, TAC, public liability |
| **Carbone Lawyers Melbourne** | Melbourne-based injury specialists with a more personal-service positioning. They say most personal-injury claims have no upfront fees and cover WorkCover, TAC, public liability and medical negligence. [www.carbonelawyers.com.au](https://www.carbonelawyers.com.au/legal-info-centre/where-to-find-a-local-personal-injury-lawyer-in-melbourne/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | If you prefer a **smaller/specialist Melbourne practice** |


**Also worth getting a quote from:** Gordon Legal Melbourne and National Compensation Lawyers. They are established Melbourne compensation practices, although I’d want to compare their actual costs agreement against the firms above before deciding.

### My pick

If it were my claim, I'd probably get **2–3 free initial consultations** rather than immediately signing with the first lawyer.

- **Best all-round comparison:** Law Partners
- **For a serious/complex claim:** Maurice Blackburn
- **For WorkCover/TAC:** Shine or Maurice Blackburn
- **For a more boutique/personal approach:** Carbone

One important warning: **“no win, no fee” does not necessarily mean “you pay nothing if you lose.”** The Victorian Legal Services Board says you can still potentially be liable for disbursements, and in some circumstances the other side's legal costs. An uplift fee can also apply, subject to Victorian limits. [lsbc.vic.gov.au](https://lsbc.vic.gov.au/consumers/legal-costs-and-billing/no-win-no-fee-cost-agreements?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

So before signing, I'd specifically ask each firm:

1. **Exactly what do I pay if we lose?**
2. **Are medical reports, barristers and other disbursements covered?**
3. **Is there an uplift fee, and how much?**
4. **What will I actually receive from a $100,000 settlement after all costs?**
5. **If the other side pays some of your costs, do I still owe anything?**

If you tell me **what type of compensation claim you have** (e.g. workplace/WorkCover, car/TAC, medical negligence, public liability, TPD, psychological injury), I can narrow this to the **3 Melbourne lawyers I'd most strongly recommend for that particular type of claim**, including their current reviews, specialist credentials and fee arrangements.
